Add a component, load a CSV, or pull the shared community pool to begin statistical quality analysis.

Scores are computed per component type, level and (at 9/10) Ship Class — each part is ranked only against like-for-like parts. The Level by toggle picks whether Looted/REed parts group by RE Level or Certification Level (Crafted always uses Cert Level — it has no RE Level). Every part gets a Best Stat headline (its strongest weighted stat, graded Bo% — position between the worst and best of its pool's range) and a Weighted Grade (the weight-averaged Bo% across its stats). Looted parts stay in their own pool per level; Crafted and REed share one "final" pool per level. Thin pools make ranges less settled, so collect more parts at each level. The Token Rarity column (Looted parts) shows how rare this good a best-stat roll is from Kash Nunes (as a 1-in-x) and the expected tokens to buy one (roll cost 50 + 5×Cert). A ⚠ RE N? flag on the level means the part's name or stats imply a different RE Level than recorded (an RE/Cert mismatch) — open the part to accept the correction.

Each cell shows a range and its colour-coded Bo% cutoffs 50% 70% 85% 95% 99% (the stat value needed to reach each quality band — hover a chip for its exact value). The Range toggle picks which: Crafted / REed shows how far each finished production path reaches so you can see when to craft vs hunt an RE — C Crafted (the crafted default seed from 161 bazaar samples + your CSV crafted rows, stretched by observed Crafted parts) and R REed (the Looted range projected up through the level's max RE bonus, stretched by observed REed parts). Crafted and REed are graded against one shared pool, so the cutoff chips beneath the two spans are a single ladder both are scored on — an RE roll is worth chasing where its span clears cutoffs the crafted span can't. Looted shows the raw-drop range (datamined, stretched by observed Looted rolls and donor values implied from your REed parts), with its own cutoffs. A top Looted roll can still reach Elite. Click a column header for the full per-level breakdown. Crafted parts group by Cert level (they have no RE level). Starting ranges & loot tables: Seraph (data.json).

RE Priorities & Suggestion Rules

Weight the stats this RE project should chase — Suggest Donors covers each weighted stat with its best owned part (best-of-each ignores the rest), so it won't waste two high-tier parts on the same stat. Defaults come from this type's Weighting; changes here apply to this project only. Once every weighted stat is maxed, extra slots are filled with your worst parts. Kuat filler is matched by name — parts with blank names (e.g. from OCR) can't be tagged Kuat.

Filler ceiling Good

Pick donor parts of the chosen type from your dataset below — only Looted parts have an RE level and are eligible donors; Crafted and already-REed parts are excluded. A Component Analysis Tool run only accepts parts that all share the same RE level, so the list below is also filtered to the RE level selected above. The projection takes the best value of each stat across the parts you select (higher/lower-is-better per stat), then applies the RE level's bonus %. Without the +10 Reverse Engineering Chance (RE Cybernetic Arm, SEAs, or RE Chance power-ups), every bonus is 1% lower. The donor count is fixed by the level, not "up to" — analyzing a level-L component takes exactly L donors (a level-1 analysis takes exactly 1, a level-10 analysis takes exactly 10); you can't add the result to your dataset until the count matches exactly.

Stat Priorities

Weight what this build should chase. Mass and reactor drain are limits, not goals — a heavier part that fits and scores higher still wins, and unused mass budget is fine. Set a weight to 0 to ignore it.

Droid Commands

Toggle the commands you intend to run; the reactor budget updates for the ones that affect it. Reactor Overload raises reactor generation; Engine Overload raises the engine's reactor drain (×1.25–10). Weapon Overload and Capacitor Overcharge are capacitor-side and aren't budgeted yet. STAT WEIGHTING

Weights scale how much each stat counts toward every part's Weighted Grade, and decide which stat becomes a part's Best Stat headline (picked by Bo% × weight). Set a weight to 0 to ignore a stat entirely.
